overview.title: CDN and caches
overview.description: Requests, errors and cache hits across every app, and which of your servers answered them.

tiles.requestsInfo: Requests the ingress handled in this time range, from request metrics.
tiles.errorsInfo: Share of requests answered with a 5xx status, including errors from the app.
tiles.hitRateInfo: Hits over hits plus misses on cached paths, for the last {{minutes}} minutes. Requests that bypass the cache are not counted.
tiles.hitRateSince: Hits over hits plus misses on cached paths. Counted in memory since the ingress started, so it resets on restart.
tiles.savedInfo: Response body bytes served from the cache instead of the app, for the last {{minutes}} minutes.
tiles.savedSince: Response body bytes served from the cache instead of the app, since the ingress started.
tiles.memoryInfo: Bytes held in the ingress against its cap. The oldest least used objects are dropped first when the cap is reached.

nodes.title: Where traffic is served from
nodes.help: Requests are counted for the server each app runs on. Visitor location is not measured.
nodes.noRegions: No region labels yet. Add one to a server on the Nodes page to see it here.
nodes.emptyTitle: No requests in this time range
nodes.emptyBody: Shares appear once an app behind a domain receives traffic.

cacheCard.title: Cache
cacheCard.help: Hits are answered by the ingress. Misses go to the app.

chart.empty: No cache activity yet. Turn caching on for a domain to see hits and misses here.
chart.aria: {{hits}} cache hits and {{misses}} misses over the last {{minutes}} minutes

caches.title: Caches
caches.description: The response cache in the ingress: how well it works for each app, and how to clear it.
caches.scopeBody: One in-memory cache in the ingress on this control plane serves every app, including apps on other servers. Purges apply there. Objects are tagged with the {{tag}} response header. Counters reset when the ingress restarts, and a per server edge cache is not available yet.
caches.chartHelp: Cache hits and misses per minute across all apps.

apps.aria: Cache hit rate by app, busiest first
apps.emptyBody: Deploy an app and give it a domain, then turn caching on.

url.title: One URL
url.help: A path and query, every variant.

tag.title: Cache tag
tag.help: Objects your app tagged in a response header.

all.title: Everything
all.help: Empties the whole cache for this scope.

purge.allNote: Removes every cached response for {{target}}. The next request to each URL goes to the app.
purge.confirmBody: Every cached response is removed from the ingress.
purge.consequenceOrigin: The app receives all requests again until the cache refills, so expect a burst of load.
purge.consequenceUndo: This cannot be undone. It is recorded in the purge history.

history.emptyBody: Purges from the dashboard, CLI or API are listed here with who ran them.

app.subtitle: Cache static files and other safe responses at the ingress so repeat requests never reach your app. Dynamic pages stay uncached unless your app or a rule allows it.
app.presetBody: Adds one rule for images, scripts, styles and fonts, and turns caching on. Your app's own Cache-Control still wins, and responses with cookies are never stored.
app.domainsAria: Cache settings for the domains of {{app}}
app.counts: {{hits}} hits, {{misses}} misses, {{bypasses}} bypassed since the ingress started.
app.noDomainsBody: The cache sits in front of domains. Add one to start caching.

redirects.title: Redirects
redirects.description: Force HTTPS, pick a canonical host and forward old addresses. Each domain has its own settings.

routing.title: Routing rules
routing.description: Send paths to another app or URL and set request and response headers. Each domain has its own settings.

controls.emptyBody: Add a domain to an app first. Its redirect and routing controls then appear here.

thirdParty.title: Using Cloudflare, Akamai or Fastly in front
thirdParty.headers: Send Cache-Control (and a tag header such as Cache-Tag) from your app. Both the CDN and the ingress follow them.
thirdParty.clientIp: Add the CDN's address ranges to the trusted proxies setting so visitor IPs, rate limits and country rules use the real client address.
thirdParty.plugins: First party integrations for CDN purge and traffic steering are planned through the plugin system. Nothing is connected today.

reasons.nextjsHelp: This looks like a Next.js app. The Next.js preset keys cached pages by its router headers.

long.vary_header: responses vary on the {{header}} header, which no cache rule lists, so they cannot be stored safely.
long.set_cookie: responses set a cookie, so they are personal and are not stored.
long.private: responses are marked private by the app.
long.no_cache: responses say no-cache, so they must be checked with the app every time.
long.status_not_cached: responses had a status the rule does not cache. Add the status to the rule to cache it.
long.too_large: responses were larger than the per object cache limit.
long.range: requests asked for part of a file (Range), which is never cached.
long.authorization: requests carried an Authorization header, so they are never cached.
long.cookie_request: requests carried a cookie. Turn on caching with cookies in the rule if the page is the same for everyone.
long.upgrade: requests asked to switch protocol (WebSocket), which is never cached.
long.other: requests were left out of the cache for less common reasons.
